feature.name: EvalCareRequestManager
feature.description: This feature specifies how EvalCare uses the ManageRequests functions to send requests to peer services and to handle requests received from them. Its four stories cover synchronous send, synchronous receive, asynchronous send, and asynchronous receive.

story.name: EvalCare Make Synchronous Request
story.description: EvalCare, on a user thread, initiates a synchronous call to a peer service and waits for the response before continuing.

requirement.name: EvalCare makes synchronous requests
requirement.requirement: EvalCare, on a user thread, MUST be able to initiate a synchronous call to a peer service and wait for the peer's response before continuing its own work.

requirement.name: EvalCare synchronous outbound payload carries User State
requirement.requirement: Every synchronous outbound request MUST take as its one and only argument either a JSON payload that EvalCare converts into a Pydantic object, or a Pydantic object directly. The payload MUST include the current User State as a first-class field. The returned response MUST be either a Pydantic object or its JSON serialization, and MUST include the User State with any modifications applied by the peer.

story.name: EvalCare Receive Synchronous Request
story.description: EvalCare, on a user thread, satisfies a synchronous request from a peer and returns the result before the peer continues its own work.

requirement.name: EvalCare satisfies synchronous requests
requirement.requirement: EvalCare, on a user thread, MUST be able to satisfy a synchronous request from a peer and return the result before the peer continues its own work.

requirement.name: EvalCare synchronous inbound payload carries User State
requirement.requirement: Every synchronous inbound request handler MUST take as its one and only argument either a JSON payload that EvalCare converts into a Pydantic object, or a Pydantic object directly. The payload MUST include the caller's current User State as a first-class field. The returned response MUST be either a Pydantic object or its JSON serialization, and MUST include the User State with any modifications applied by EvalCare.

story.name: EvalCare Make Asynchronous Request
story.description: EvalCare initiates an asynchronous call to a peer service and continues without waiting; the response is delivered later via a callback EvalCare supplies.

requirement.name: EvalCare makes asynchronous requests
requirement.requirement: EvalCare MUST be able to initiate an asynchronous call to a peer service and continue its own work without waiting for the peer's response.

requirement.name: EvalCare asynchronous outbound payload carries User State
requirement.requirement: Every asynchronous outbound request MUST take as its one and only argument either a JSON payload that EvalCare converts into a Pydantic object, or a Pydantic object directly. The payload MUST include the current User State as a first-class field. The delivered response MUST be either a Pydantic object or its JSON serialization, and MUST include the User State with any modifications applied by the peer.

requirement.name: EvalCare asynchronous outbound supplies a callback mechanism
requirement.requirement: Every asynchronous outbound request MUST supply a callback mechanism through which the peer's response is delivered. The callback mechanism MUST be an API endpoint, an in-memory event, or both.

story.name: EvalCare Receive Asynchronous Request
story.description: EvalCare accepts an asynchronous request, allows the peer to continue, and later delivers the response via the caller-supplied callback.

requirement.name: EvalCare accepts asynchronous requests
requirement.requirement: EvalCare MUST be able to accept an asynchronous request from a peer and produce the response after the caller has continued its own work.

requirement.name: EvalCare asynchronous inbound payload carries User State
requirement.requirement: Every asynchronous inbound request handler MUST take as its one and only argument either a JSON payload that EvalCare converts into a Pydantic object, or a Pydantic object directly. The payload MUST include the caller's current User State as a first-class field. The delivered response MUST be either a Pydantic object or its JSON serialization, and MUST include the User State with any modifications applied by EvalCare.

requirement.name: EvalCare asynchronous inbound delivers via caller's callback mechanism
requirement.requirement: The response MUST be delivered to the caller through the callback mechanism the caller supplied in the original request. The callback mechanism MUST be an API endpoint, an in-memory event, or both.

feature.name: Manage ChatHealthy's 0 Trust security
feature.description: End-to-end identity, certificate, and authentication rules for every entity that authenticates against ChatHealthy.ai: end users, operators, services, containers, pipeline components, external clients. The feature owns the ChatHealthy certificate authority, the session-token envelope carried between components, OAuth login for humans, the User State object, mutual authentication rules, and the identity registry that binds every authenticating actor to a canonical identity.

story.name: GUID â€” stable per-session auth credential
story.description: The stable 32-char session identifier carried inside the security token. Manufactured once per page session and preserved across every cross-service hop.

story.name: NONCE â€” fresh-per-hop replay defense
story.description: The 17-char timestamp stamped freshly by every server on receive. Defends against replay per NIST 800-53 SC-23. Distinct from the GUID; only the nonce changes per hop.

requirement.requirement: The NONCE value displayed in the session-verification panel MUST reflect the most recent stamping done on behalf of the currently-owning service. Ownership belongs to the service whose UI the user is interacting with: FindCare drives the Left Panel; EvaluateCare or SharedServices drives the Right Panel. The contacted server for all browser traffic is always SharedServices /gate per EPIC-002-F-004-S-001; the displayed-owner is independent of the contacted gateway and is determined by which iframe holds the active view.
requirement.name: Displayed-service ownership determines which panel shows the most recent nonce stamp

story.name: Security Token â€” signed wire envelope
story.description: The wire object and its content exchanged between services: { origin, token (CH{nonce}{created}{guid}), signature, created_at, signed, server_env }. Binds the GUID and nonce under an RSA PKCS1v15 SHA256 signature by the current stamping origin.

requirement.requirement: The session token MUST be a single object that carries the session GUID (S-001-REQ-T-001), the session nonce (S-002-REQ-T-002), and a cryptographic signature over the GUID and nonce. The token MUST also carry an origin field identifying the ChatHealthy component that produced this instance of the token. This requirement is the single source of truth for token format; all other stories reference this REQ rather than restating token structure.
requirement.name: Session token format

requirement.requirement: (Deferred by operator.) Session token mutual authentication MUST pass for SharedServices. The same token FindCare created MUST be the same one SharedServices received.
requirement.name: Enforce SharedServices mutual auth using FindCare-created session token

requirement.requirement: The origin field on any returned session token MUST identify the component that produced this response, distinct from the cryptographic signer of any embedded content.
requirement.name: Origin field identifies this response's sender

requirement.requirement: The session token display MUST separate the nonce from the GUID so a human can visually verify each part. The display MUST show: (1) Signed token (the encrypted signature), (2) Nonce (the two timestamps extracted from the token), (3) GUID (the session identifier extracted from the token). The nonce and GUID MUST be displayed as separate labeled fields. The presentation in the right panel (after EvaluateCare or SharedServices handoff) MUST be identical to the presentation in the left panel. Both panels MUST use the same labels, layout, and format.
requirement.name: Signed-token panel renders signed token, nonce, GUID as separate labeled fields, identical in both panels

requirement.requirement: The session-verification widget MUST display the time in UTC.
requirement.name: Time displayed in UTC
Mutual TLS for every cross-service and external system-to-system call
requirement.requirement: Every call between two ChatHealthy components, and every external system-to-system client request to any ChatHealthy service, MUST be authenticated via mutual TLS before any application-layer payload is exchanged or processed. The authentication MUST identify the client to the service. Only the client that sent the request and the service that receives it may have access to the request's contents. A failed or incomplete handshake MUST be a fatal error. If a component cannot fulfill this requirement in its current substrate, a bug MUST be registered against it. Realization at the transport layer for any component the substrate cannot host is governed by BUG-004.

story.name: Create and login users with OAuth across supported identity providers
story.description: ChatHealthy.ai MUST support the creation and use of identity-provider IDs (Google, Facebook, Apple, and others as introduced) for logins using each identity provider's OAuth capabilities. The firm and its application rely on identity providers as identity sources. This story specifies all the technical and business requirements for this capability.

requirement.name: Human identity is sourced from OAuth identity providers
requirement.requirement: ChatHealthy MUST support human login via each supported identity provider's OAuth 2.0 flow. New identity providers MUST be added by declaration. No human authentication path other than OAuth 2.0 MAY exist.

requirement.name: Login and registration navigation entry
requirement.requirement: Every static ChatHealthy page MUST offer a Login and Registration entry point in the top-level navigation. Clicking it MUST initiate the OAuth flow at the user-selected identity provider.

requirement.name: OAuth callback creates or reconciles the user record
requirement.requirement: On a successful OAuth callback, the system MUST identify the human as either returning or new. Returning humans MUST be reconciled to their existing user record by matching the identity-provider identity and, failing that, by the identity provider's verified email. New humans MUST have a new user record created. Every user record MUST record every identity-provider identity ever used to log the human in.

requirement.name: Successful login surfaces user status
requirement.requirement: On successful login the system MUST tell the human they are logged in. On a first login the human MUST be welcomed as a new user. On a return login the human MUST be welcomed back and told when they last logged in.

requirement.name: Guest conversation preserved on return login
requirement.requirement: When a returning human logs in, the conversation the guest User State was carrying MUST be appended to the stored user's conversation history before the stored User State replaces the guest User State.

requirement.name: Failed authentication preserves guest state
requirement.requirement: On a failed authentication the system MUST keep the human as a guest, MUST inform them the authentication failed, MUST NOT delete any user record, and MUST NOT disclose whether the identity is known to ChatHealthy.

requirement.name: Login attempts and outcomes are audited
requirement.requirement: Every login attempt and its outcome MUST be recorded in the ChatHealthy security audit stream, together with the identity provider, the identity used, and the outcome.

requirement.name: Frontend follows redirect events
requirement.requirement: On any /gate NDJSON event of shape {"type": "redirect", "url": <string>}, the frontend consumer MUST call window.location.assign(<url>).

requirement.name: End-to-end login test
requirement.requirement: An end-to-end automated test MUST exercise the full login and registration sequence and MUST assert every screen and message the human sees during that sequence. The test MUST be part of the regression suite.

requirement.name: Authorization is layered on OIDC atop OAuth 2.0
requirement.requirement: Every authorization decision made about a human authenticated by an identity provider MUST be driven by OpenID Connect (OIDC) claims layered over the OAuth 2.0 authentication result. OAuth 2.0 by itself MUST NOT be used to make authorization decisions. The OIDC layer MUST be sourced from a supported open-source library or supported identity-provider surface; no ChatHealthy code MAY implement OIDC token verification from scratch.

requirement.name: Registration creates the users record
requirement.requirement: When no existing users record carries { identity_provider: <identity provider>, identity_provider_user_id: <identity-provider user ID> } in its OAuthIdentities AND no existing OAuthIdentities[].email matches the verified email returned by this callback, the SharedServices /auth/<identity_provider>/callback endpoint MUST create a new users record (a UserObject) with: user_id set to a freshly generated random GUID (RFC 4122 UUIDv4); OAuthIdentities set to exactly one entry { identity_provider: <identity provider>, identity_provider_user_id: <identity-provider user ID>, email: <identity-provider email> }; public_username set to the verified email returned by the identity provider (this default value may be changed by the user via a future story); is_registered = True; user_type = "Prospect".

requirement.name: Persist mirrors user_object to the users collection when is_registered == True
requirement.requirement: AuthorizationsAndAuthenticationsTool.persist() MUST, on every invocation, write the current user_object to admin.sessions (keyed by GUID). When the user_object's is_registered == True, persist() MUST ALSO write the same user_object to the users collection (keyed by user_id). The two writes MUST carry the same UserObject value.

requirement.name: UserObject defines OAuthIdentities, an array of identity-provider identities
requirement.requirement: The UserObject schema MUST define a field named OAuthIdentities of type array. Each array element MUST be an object with exactly three sub-fields: (a) identity_provider - the identity-provider name; the enum is open and includes each supported identity provider (initially "Google", with additional identity providers added as introduced); (b) identity_provider_user_id - the identity provider's stable identifier for the user; (c) email - the verified email returned by the identity provider on its most recent OAuth callback for this user. The array MUST be non-empty whenever is_registered == True.

requirement.name: Cross-identity-provider reconciliation via verified email
requirement.requirement: On every successful OAuth callback, the endpoint MUST first attempt to match (identity_provider, identity_provider_user_id) against any user_object.OAuthIdentities entry across the users collection. When that match succeeds, the returning-login path per EPIC-002-F-003-S-004-REQ-T-012 runs. Otherwise, the endpoint MUST attempt to match the verified email returned by this callback against any user_object.OAuthIdentities[].email. When that match succeeds, the endpoint MUST append { identity_provider, identity_provider_user_id, email } to that user's OAuthIdentities, replace the current session's guest user_object with the stored UserObject, and bind that stored UserObject to the current session. Otherwise, the registration path per EPIC-002-F-003-S-004-REQ-T-009 runs.

requirement.name: Pre-alpha authorized-registrant allow-list is hardcoded in application code
requirement.requirement: The pre-alpha allow-list of authorized registrants MUST be 100% hardcoded in the application code. No database collection, no env var, no manifest entry â€” to add or remove an authorized pre-alpha user the operator edits the code and redeploys.

story.name: User State
story.description: Defines the User State object â€” the in-session and post-session representation of a ChatHealthy user.

requirement.requirement: Every ChatHealthy session MUST instantiate exactly one User State object at session start. For logged-in humans the object is loaded from persistent storage; for guests the object is created fresh.
requirement.name: One User State per session

requirement.requirement: The structure of every User State document MUST conform to the canonical ChatHealthy User State schema. Any divergence MUST be a fatal error.
requirement.name: User State schema is authoritative
User State flows on every stateful request and response
requirement.requirement: Every stateful request and response between ChatHealthy components MUST carry the current User State as a first-class field. Modifications made by any hop MUST be returned to the caller.

depends_on.reason: Session-token assembly per REQ-B-007.
Most-recent-restamp timestamp per REQ-B-002.

requirement.name: Session token accompanies the User State
requirement.requirement: The session token defined by S-003-REQ-B-001 MUST accompany every request that carries a User State. The token, not the User State body, is the authentication credential; the User State is the payload the credential protects.

requirement.name: Session boot on every page load
requirement.requirement: Every page load of any ChatHealthy client surface MUST perform a session-boot call to SharedServices as its first network action. The response MUST establish or refresh the User State and the session token for that page.

depends_on.reason: REQ-B-001 defines the 67-byte session-token assembly.

requirement.name: Session lifetime surfaces to the client
requirement.requirement: The server MUST surface to the client, on every response, how much of the session lifetime remains. The client MUST refuse to issue a new request when the remaining lifetime has fallen below zero. Expired sessions MUST return the user to a fresh guest state.

story.name: Certificate authority and certificate lifecycle
story.description: ChatHealthy operates its own PKI authority. The authority issues certificates on demand and in real time, and makes each certificate and its associated key material available to authorized users through an interface secured by the requester's identity.

requirement.name: ChatHealthy operates its own certificate authority; use by components is optional
requirement.requirement: ChatHealthy MUST operate its own certificate authority and MUST make it available to every ChatHealthy component that elects to authenticate against a ChatHealthy-issued certificate. Use of the ChatHealthy-operated authority is OPTIONAL: a component MAY authenticate using a certificate issued by a recognized third-party authority when the component's operating context requires it. Every certificate ChatHealthy's authority issues remains subject to the traceability, authorization, and lifecycle rules in this story.

requirement.name: Every issued certificate is traceable to its identity, network node, and server
requirement.requirement: Every chatHealthy.ai certificate the authority issues MUST be traceable to the identity, the network node, and the chatHealthy.ai server to which it is associated. Certificates lacking an identifiable subject, network node, or server association MUST NOT be issued. The authority MUST issue a certificate only to an authorized requester whose own identity is verified and who holds an entitlement to obtain a certificate for the requested subject; requests from unverified or unentitled requesters MUST be refused.

requirement.name: Certificate provisioning matches identity lifetime; job-scoped destruction
requirement.requirement: Long-lived identities MUST receive a certificate at the moment the identity is brought into existence. Short-lived identities MUST self-mint a certificate at the moment they come into existence. A certificate's validity MUST end no later than the identity it belongs to ceases to exist. Long-lived certificates MUST expire on a schedule short enough that a compromise cannot outlive a single management cycle, but long enough that a certificate expiring during an unexpectedly long job will not occur. It is permissible to accomplish this by issuing short-term certificates valid for up to a week; when the job for which such certificates were issued completes, every certificate associated with that job MUST be revoked and destroyed from every place it exists.

story.name: Private-credential custody and authorized retrieval
story.description: This story specifies who or what CAN obtain a private credential, who audits every retrieval, and how least privilege is enforced on both machine and human identities.

requirement.name: Private credentials are held only by their issued identity
requirement.requirement: The private component of every certificate MUST be readable only by the identity to which the certificate was issued. Every retrieval MUST authenticate the caller as that identity before returning the material.

requirement.name: Least privilege on secrets
requirement.requirement: Every secret required by any ChatHealthy component or human operator MUST be readable only by that party. No party MAY hold read access to a secret it does not require to perform its declared function.

story.name: System-to-system identity management
story.description: The identity model for every non-human ChatHealthy component that authenticates. Every authenticating component has one canonical identity, and every identity, machine or human, lives in a single registry.

requirement.name: One canonical identity per authenticating component
requirement.requirement: Every non-human ChatHealthy component that authenticates MUST have exactly one canonical identity. That identity MUST be the same on every surface at which the component authenticates.

requirement.name: Single authoritative identity registry
requirement.requirement: Every canonical identity MUST be declared in a single authoritative registry maintained by ChatHealthy. Every identity, machine or human, MUST appear in this registry. No component or human MAY authenticate under an identity not in the registry.

requirement.name: New identities require human approval
requirement.requirement: New identities MUST NOT be created ad hoc. Every proposed new identity MUST be authored by Claude Code and MUST be approved by a human operator before it enters the registry and receives a certificate.

requirement.name: Registry entry names every authenticating surface
requirement.requirement: Each identity's registry entry MUST enumerate every surface at which the identity is entitled to authenticate.

requirement.name: Least-privilege scoping of every identity
requirement.requirement: No identity MAY hold privileges beyond those required for its declared function.

requirement.name: Authorization mechanism MUST comply with OAuth 2.0 and OIDC
requirement.requirement: The mechanism ChatHealthy uses to authorize the surfaces enumerated by REQ-B-004 MUST comply with OAuth 2.0 and OpenID Connect (OIDC). ChatHealthy MUST NOT implement its own authorization framework: the substrate MUST be either a supported identity-provider surface (for example an Entra authorization capability) or a recognized open-source library that implements OAuth 2.0 and OIDC. The specific substrate choice is recorded on the F-003 design document; this requirement fixes the compliance surface.

feature.name: Universal Navigation
feature.description: The ChatHealthy.ai application guides users to find care, evaluate their choices objectively, and meet with their loved ones, care providers, and AI robots to discuss their options, and potentially get deep research based on their context. Users might be registered, guests, customers, or site administrators. The requirements for One Universal Navigation Mechanism are specified herein. Navigation takes place between an end user typing values into a prompt or using one of ChatHealthy's tools and corresponding UX component to do work such as picking providers, specialties, clinical trials, or tuning the mixing board in EvaluateCare. These requirements when met must, along with other controls, demonstrate ChatHealthy's compliance with NIST 800-53. I.e., they must meet the strictest requirements that any HIPAA audit might uncover.

story.name: Universal entrance: all ChatHealthy.ai client to server calls route through SharedServices /gate
story.description: The single client-facing endpoint for the entire ChatHealthy.ai application is SharedServices /gate. Every browser-initiated HTTP call from any ChatHealthy.ai surface - the wrapper site, embedded FindCare/EvaluateCare iframes, future mobile webviews, future native clients - funnels through this one endpoint. SharedServices performs any cross-component work server-to-server on behalf of the client.

requirement.name: All calls to ChatHealthy.ai MUST go to the ChatHealthy.ai Universal Gate
requirement.requirement: All browser, or other client, calls to ChatHealthy.ai servers MUST POST to {env}.sharedservices.chathealthy.ai/gate. Other calls to other URLs, except for the domain name by itself, MUST result in a 404; i.e., calls to http://chathealthy.ai, https://chathealthy.ai, http://dev.chathealthy.ai, https://dev.chathealthy.ai, http://qa.chathealthy.ai, https://qa.chathealthy.ai MUST all redirect to the universal gate call.

requirement.name: Skip already-completed upstream work on follow-up turns
requirement.requirement: When the Utterance Manager (UM) upgrades target_action on a follow-up turn because a pending_disambiguation just resolved, the Universal Router (UR) does not re-run any upstream tool whose result is already cached on the IntentDocument. UR reads the cached output from the relevant intent entry's arguments and dispatches only the downstream tool that still needs to run. Asking the user a clarification question therefore does not pay the cost of re-classifying or re-fetching upstream work the user has already seen.

depends_on.reason: Depends on UM's pending_disambiguation state per REQ-B-007 and REQ-B-009.

requirement.name: IntentDocument carries upstream tool outputs across turns
requirement.requirement: Each typed intent entry in the IntentDocument carries the outputs of upstream tools as additional arguments. The Universal Router (UR) writes these arguments after the upstream tool runs the first time and reads them on follow-up turns to satisfy REQ-B-002. The schema for each intent entry enumerates the upstream-output arguments it accepts so the contract between the Utterance Manager (UM), UR, and each consuming tool is explicit.

requirement.name: Serial wire order on partial-information turns
requirement.requirement: On a turn that carries both a user_message and a partial-information target_action, the wire order is deterministic. The Utterance Manager (UM) streams its {kind:"prompt"} event and awaits an event-loop tick to flush before returning to the Universal Router (UR). UR then dispatches downstream tools per target_action; each tool streams its own events and flushes before returning. UR emits its terminal {kind:"final"}. UR does not chain to closeConnection200 on a turn that carries a pending disambiguation, because the connection is logically still open across the user's next turn.

depends_on.reason: Depends on UM REQ-B-009 (user_message field) and REQ-B-010 (LLM authors prose).

requirement.name: Universal Router handles authentication by calling OAuthLoginTool directly
requirement.requirement: In order to support testing in the localhost environment, the Universal Router MUST handle the authentication flow by calling OAuthLoginTool directly. The Universal Router MUST NOT route the authentication flow through the UtteranceManager. This is the natural flow in all other environments.

story.name: Implement unique FindCare Universal Router requirements
story.description: This story specifies the Universal Router (UR) behavior that is specific to FindCare's two action types â€” findAProvider and specialtySearch â€” beyond what the general Universal Router story (EPIC-002-F-004-S-001) defines. It covers the SpecialtyFilter output as the cached upstream result carried as nucc_codes on each FindCare intent entry, the UR-side write and re-read of nucc_codes across turns so SpecialtyFilter does not run twice on the same complaint, and the schema sufficiency rule that gates UR dispatch of ProviderSearch so the provider search executes only when geography is fully specified. story.name: Session Coordination for Stateful Work
story.description: Every stateful call from a client to the gateway is coordinated through the calling thread. Parallel state-changing work from a client to the gateway is disallowed by design; the user experiences the resulting serialization as a real wait. The server MAY route calls to peer servers in parallel when necessary.

requirement.name: Calling thread owns the merge

requirement.name: No parallel state-changing work

feature.name: Utterance Tool
feature.description: This feature defines the requirements for the handling of every user interaction with ChatHealthy.ai's core front-end application that requires LLM-mediated routing or prose. The Utterance Manager (UM) has two responsibilities. (a) Interpret â€” when the user types free-text into the prompt, UM classifies the latest utterance, builds the canonical IntentDocument, and may author a user_message prompt the user back. This is the 'interpret an utterance' path. (b) Manufacture â€” when the user clicks a structured UI control (Apply Filter, future selected-for-evaluation gates, future pagination edges) that requires the system to ask the user something before it can act, the Universal Router (UR) dispatches UM with a synthetic trigger. UM reads the carried IntentDocument's slot state and authors a brief LLM-generated user_message requesting whatever slot is missing. No free-text utterance was typed; UM is manufacturing an utterance the system needs to deliver. Both paths end the same way: UM writes an IntentDocument back to user_object.intent, optionally streams user_message as kind:'prompt', and returns. UR validates and dispatches the resulting target_action. This feature is complete when every user-facing chat prose in the application is either (a) interpreted from a free-text utterance via path (a) or (b) manufactured by UM via path (b) â€” and no tool authors its own chat strings.

story.name: Universal utterance routing
story.description: The single canonical routing path for every user utterance from the input control through to the terminal user_object update. Holds the business rule that all utterances flow through this path and the technical contract for each hop in the path.

requirement.name: All user utterances must flow through the user-prompt tool
requirement.requirement: Every user prompt coming from any component, e.g. user-prompt input, where a user uses natural language to communicate with the app MUST flow through the UniversalNavigationTool to the UtteranceManager.

requirement.name: Tool input is a Pydantic object that carries User State
requirement.requirement: The tool's input MUST be a Pydantic object (or its JSON serialization) that includes the current User State as a first-class field. The User State conforms to the canonical schema defined by EPIC-002-F-003 (Authorizations and Authentications).

depends_on.reason: Defines the canonical User State / User Object

requirement.name: Tool must be tightly coupled with a front end component
requirement.requirement: The tool MUST be tightly coupled with a front-end JS file that: (1) takes the input from the user and sends it to the universal router using the universal router's input pydantic tool as a JSON; if and only if the router determines that it was an utterance shall the router construct the pydantic object and pass it to the tool. The component MUST be capable of both transmitting the user's input and responding in text if further natural language input is required from the user.

depends_on.reason: Universal Navigation feature â€” defines the universal router

requirement.name: UtteranceManager obtains tool metadata from the router and caches it at runtime
requirement.requirement: UtteranceManager MUST obtain downstream-tool metadata from the universal router's metadata API. UtteranceManager MUST cache the retrieved metadata at runtime â€” the API call is for cache population on startup (or on cache invalidation), not a per-utterance lookup. The router's registry is the source of truth; UtteranceManager holds a runtime copy.

requirement.name: Multi-thread processing is limited to non-state-changing operations
requirement.requirement: The universal utterance tool must be capable of multi-threaded processing for non-state-changing operations (Mongo reads, LLM calls). Within that multithreaded environment, if a precedence thread returns before other threads complete, the tool must be capable of invoking a downstream tool without waiting for the other threads. Parallel processing MUST NOT include state-changing writes to shared user state; the no-parallel-state-changing-work rule (EPIC-002-F-004-S-004-REQ-B-002) and the one-in-flight-per-user rule (EPIC-002-F-004-S-004-REQ-B-003) govern any stateful calls.

requirement.name: Classifier input is the last N user utterances
requirement.requirement: The Utterance Manager (UM) classifier input is up to the last 10 user utterances drawn from user_object.session_conversation_history.utterances. The cap is a maximum, not a target â€” fewer turns are passed when the session has not accumulated that many. Tool-invocation entries and LLM-clarification bridge entries are excluded from the window so the classifier sees only what the human said.

requirement.name: Ambiguous-but-resolvable third action state
requirement.requirement: The Utterance Manager (UM) classifier distinguishes three states for any required action slot: sufficient, missing, and ambiguous-with-candidate. Ambiguous-with-candidate applies when the slot cannot be filled from the utterance alone but the classifier has a plausible candidate value for it. In this state UM sets target_action to the partial-information action so any work that does not depend on the missing slot can still proceed, records the candidate value as pending_disambiguation on the relevant intent entry, and emits an LLM-authored user_message proposing the candidate to the user.

requirement.name: Pending disambiguation resolved on the next turn
requirement.requirement: When the next utterance is a yes/no answer to the prior pending disambiguation, the Utterance Manager (UM) resolves it. "Yes" fills the candidate value into the appropriate argument on the IntentDocument and upgrades target_action to the now-fully-specified action. "No" keeps target_action at the partial-information action and emits a follow-up LLM-authored user_message requesting the missing slot a different way. Either outcome clears the prior pending_disambiguation.

requirement.name: IntentDocument carries disambiguation state and user-facing prose
requirement.requirement: The canonical IntentDocument has two optional fields beyond its required target_action and intents. The first is pending_disambiguation, attached per-intent on each entry in intents[], an object that captures the disambiguation kind, the candidate value being proposed, and any scaffolding the next-turn resolver needs; it persists across turns until the Utterance Manager (UM) clears it. The second is user_message, attached at the top level of the IntentDocument, a string carrying the LLM's prose intended for the user; when it is non-empty UM streams it as {kind:"prompt", data:{text: user_message}} and flushes before returning to the Universal Router (UR), when it is absent UM streams nothing.

requirement.name: LLM authors all user-facing chat prose
requirement.requirement: The Utterance Manager (UM) classifier's structured output includes a user_message field. The LLM writes every user-facing chat line â€” clarification questions, follow-ups, friendly framing, error explanations â€” and UM streams whatever the LLM produced. No hardcoded clarification or chat string appears in UM, CloseConnection200Tool, or any other component on the dispatch path. The LLM owns the prose; the runtime owns the transport.

requirement.name: Classifier prompt corrects significant misspellings or asks when uncertain
requirement.requirement: If a spelling error is significant to understanding an utterance, the Utterance Manager classifier prompt MUST treat user-typed misspellings as a first-class case. For each suspected significant misspelling: if the classifier is at least 75% confident of the intended word, it MUST substitute the corrected form into the output fields (e.g. complaint, geography.city, geography.state, geography.county etc.) and proceed with the normal classification rules. On the same turn the classifier MUST populate BOTH (a) a structured corrections[] list on its output containing one {"original": <user-typed word>, "corrected": <corrected word>} entry per substitution applied, AND (b) user_message set to the user's full corrected utterance with each correction annotated inline in the form <corrected_word> (corrected from '<original>') using straight single quotes. The two outputs MUST be consistent: every corrections[] entry MUST appear in user_message as a (corrected from '...') marker and vice versa. The frontend uses the corrections[] list (not text-parsing of user_message) to identify and render each marker in red font, so the user sees that their spelling was interpreted, not ignored. If confidence is below 75%, the classifier MUST NOT guess; it MUST set target_action="closeConnection200" and emit a brief user_message naming up to three plausible candidates and asking the user to clarify; corrections[] MUST be empty in that case.

requirement.name: User utterances MUST NOT propagate a fatal exception
requirement.requirement: No user utterance â€” regardless of content, length, language, malformedness, ambiguity, or spelling â€” CAN cause the Utterance Manager to propagate a fatal application exception to the user. The classifier MUST always produce a valid IntentDocument with a usable target_action (typically closeConnection200 with a brief friendly clarification when no other action can be derived). No exception within the Utterance Manager tool can throw. Any unhandled exception inside UM MUST be caught within the UM tool and converted to an appropriate user message.

requirement.name: UtteranceManager does not handle the authentication flow
requirement.requirement: The UtteranceManager MUST NOT handle the authentication flow. This is an explicit exception per EPIC-002-F-004-S-001-REQ-B-005.

depends_on.reason: Anchors the explicit exception cited by this requirement.

story.name: Implement unique FindCare Utterance Manager requirements
story.description: This story specifies the Utterance Manager (UM) behavior that is specific to FindCare's two action types â€” findAProvider and specialtySearch â€” beyond what the general Utterance Manager story (EPIC-002-F-010-S-001) defines. It covers the geography slot as the ambiguous-but-resolvable disambiguation slot when the user names a city or county without a state, the UM-side handling of the corresponding pending_disambiguation marker on the IntentDocument's findAProvider intent entry, and the LLM-authored user_message proposing the candidate state to the user. UM behavior shared with non-FindCare actions (closeConnection200) is out of scope for this story.

requirement.name: Geography slot is the disambiguation slot for findAProvider
requirement.requirement: For the findAProvider action, the geography slot uses the general ambiguous-but-resolvable pattern defined in Utterance Manager (UM) REQ-B-007. When the SpecialtyFilter has produced NUCC codes but UM has only a city or county without state, the IntentDocument's IntentFindAProvider entry carries the candidate state on pending_disambiguation, target_action remains at specialtySearch so the filter still renders, and UM proposes the candidate via user_message.

depends_on.reason: Instantiates the general ambiguous-but-resolvable pattern from REQ-B-007 and the schema additions from REQ-B-009.

requirement.name: Apply Filter with insufficient geography routes through UM as a manufacture turn
requirement.requirement: When UR receives op='apply_filter' with a payload containing the new nucc_codes set, UR reads the carried IntentDocument's geography from user_object.intent. If geography is sufficient (per the same sufficiency rule findAProvider applies â€” zip, state, state+city, or state+county), UR builds the IntentDocument deterministically with target_action=findAProvider using the new nucc_codes set, and dispatches ProviderSearch without calling UM. If geography is insufficient, UR populates a manufacture_utterance_reason dict with at minimum gesture='apply_filter' and missing_slot='geography', optionally adds session-derived facts (prior complaint, prior partial geography candidate, etc.) it deems useful, and dispatches UM as a manufacture-trigger Request per EPIC-002-F-010-S-003. UR does NOT specify the prose; UM authors it per EPIC-002-F-010-S-003-REQ-B-003.

depends_on.reason: Depends on the manufacture-trigger Request schema (REQ-T-001), the always-end-in-closeConnection200 rule (REQ-B-002), and the context-sensitive prose rule (REQ-B-003).

story.name: Manufacture utterances for non-free-text triggers
story.description: Defines UM's manufacture-path responsibility. When UR receives a structured UI gesture instead of a free-text utterance, UR dispatches UM with a synthetic trigger Request carrying a structured manufacture_utterance_reason â€” a set of hardcoded, non-user-facing facts UR has assembled about why a manufactured utterance is needed (e.g., gesture='apply_filter', missing_slot='geography', plus any session-state facts UR thinks relevant). UM uses a distinct, narrower prompt template that takes those facts AND the prior dialogue from session_conversation_history and authors a brief user-facing user_message sensitive to the conversational context â€” NOT a phrase the operator could have hardcoded. UM then morphs the IntentDocument's target_action to closeConnection200 (the user-facing prose is the answer for this turn; the user's next free-text utterance comes back through the interpret path and resolves any pending slot via the normal disambiguation mechanism). The manufacture prompt is distinct from the classifier prompt and is governed by its own output schema constraints.

requirement.name: UM accepts two trigger types
requirement.requirement: UM's Request shape carries a discriminator field trigger_type with values 'utterance' (the free-text classifier path) and 'manufacture' (the manufacture path). When trigger_type='utterance' UM reads the latest person utterance from user_object.session_conversation_history and runs the classifier prompt as today. When trigger_type='manufacture' UM does NOT read free-text; it reads the synthetic trigger context off the Request and runs the manufacture prompt. UM's Response shape is unchanged â€” an IntentDocument written to user_object.intent.

requirement.name: Manufacture path uses a distinct prompt template that always ends in closeConnection200
requirement.requirement: The manufacture prompt is narrower than the classifier prompt: it does not classify intents (the manufacture trigger and reason already name the intent context), it authors a brief user-facing user_message responsive to the supplied manufacture_utterance_reason and the prior dialogue. Hardcoded chat strings remain forbidden everywhere; the LLM authors all manufacture-path user_message text. After authoring the user_message, UM MUST set target_action=closeConnection200 on the emitted IntentDocument â€” the manufactured utterance IS the turn's answer; UR closes the connection and the user's next free-text utterance returns through the interpret path. The IntentDocument's intents[] array may carry forward intent entries (e.g. cached nucc_codes, partial geography, pending_disambiguation markers) so the next-turn interpret path can resolve naturally; only the target_action is constrained.

depends_on.reason: Builds on the LLM-authored-prose rule (REQ-B-010) and the IntentDocument shape (REQ-B-009).

requirement.name: Manufactured user_message must be context-sensitive, not formulaic
requirement.requirement: The manufacture path EXISTS because the user-facing prose is too context-dependent to hardcode. UM's manufacture prompt MUST consult the prior dialogue (recent transcript window) AND the manufacture_utterance_reason facts together when authoring the user_message. The result must read as a natural continuation of the conversation, not as a generic templated phrase. A prose output that ignores prior dialogue and could have been hardcoded in UR is a regression on this REQ â€” the whole reason the path is LLM-mediated is that UR cannot author this prose deterministically.

epic.description: This epic defines all of the services that are shared by the ChatHealthy.AI runtime application used by consumers, and site administrators. This includes functional shared services such as universal navigation services, security services, safety services, etc.

epic.name: ChatHealthy FrontEnd libary
epic.description: Shared Python library distributed as the pip package `chathealthy-lib` (repo root: `ChatHealthyLib/`). Owns the code consumed in common by ChatHealthy.ai's front-end-facing services (FindCare, EvaluateCare, SharedServices) and the wrapper. Scope is FRONT-END application code only â€” devops, data pipelines, and analytics are explicitly out of scope. Operating-model intent: a separate team with its own P&L manages this library; consumers depend on it via versioned releases (`pip install chathealthy-lib==X.Y.Z`) following standard industry convention for shared libraries, including the boundary that the package mints no auth tokens â€” auth-token MANUFACTURE belongs 100% to SharedServices; only auth-token MANAGEMENT (verification, parsing, nonce advancement) is shared and lives here.

feature.name: Shared front-end UX widget library
feature.description: Distribution mechanism + source-of-truth for the display-only UX widgets currently inlined in Website/index.html and the FindCare React iframe. Includes the chFatalError full-screen overlay, the non-prod env banner, the non-prod security panel (right-side rightSecurity panel), and any future widget shared by more than one front-end consumer. The library carries NO business logic â€” peer selection, mutual-auth pairing, service routing, ownership state, and any other biz-logic concerns are explicitly excluded and live in the backend per the no-biz-logic-on-client rule. Distribution channel TBD (npm package, CDN-hosted versioned bundle, or repo-internal copy at deploy time) â€” to be decided as part of the first story under this feature. Owned by the same EPIC-003 team that owns chathealthy-lib (Python).

feature.name: Backend orchestration that supports the shared front-end UX widgets
feature.description: Backend endpoints + service-layer code that own all the business logic that today lives inline in Website/index.html and the FindCare React iframe â€” peer selection (which backend's /health to call), mutual-auth pairing (the /session-then-/verify-token sequence currently driven from the wrapper), service-routing/ownership-state (gotoFindCare/gotoEvaluateCare/gotoSharedServices and the underlying ownership transition), and any other biz-logic decision the wrapper is making today. The widgets in EPIC-003-F-001 then become pure display: each widget consumes ONE clean data endpoint per render. This feature exists so that the no-biz-logic-on-client rule can actually be enforced; without it, extracting widgets only relocates the violation, not removes it. Per the auth caveat, token MANUFACTURE belongs 100% to SharedServices and any orchestration here MUST respect that boundary.
realized_by: sharedServices/Code/ (likely host of the orchestration endpoints)

feature.name: Manage Errors
feature.description: This feature defines the requirements to manage errors that the ChatHealthy.ai's application code encounters. It defines a unified deliberate-exception model across the ChatHealthy.ai codebase. Every exception explicitly managed shares an exception class â€” ChatHealthyException. This exception class has a mode discriminator and structured context dict. Catch sites discriminate on mode, not on exception type. External exceptions (httpx, pymongo, etc.) remain as their native types and are converted to ChatHealthyException at well-defined boundaries. The default behavior is and remains, when an exception occurs, fail hard and fast. But that policy is mitigated by the need to handle expected errors from users and external systems gracefully.

It shows identity, credentials, every practice and business address (labeled and ordered), every license, insurance identifiers, the pipeline-derived enrichments (county info, urban marker), and external research links the user can click to verify the provider independently. Every field is read from the provider record in our Mongo; that record is brought to live-NPPES freshness on each click by the data-management story (EPIC-006-F-002-S-002).

requirement.name: Pipeline-enriched county info shown per address
requirement.requirement: For every address row the panel MUST display the county name (from county.name on the address) and the urban marker (from county.urban). When county.urban is absent on an address (e.g. a just-written-back new address whose urban workbook pass has not yet re-run) the panel renders the county name only, no urban marker. The county.fips and county.source fields are internal â€” not shown to the user.

requirement.name: Insurance section from the normalized insurance[] array
requirement.requirement: The panel MUST display an Insurance section rendering every entry in the record's normalized insurance[] array. Each row shows the insurance_type (human-readable, e.g. 'Medicaid', 'Medicare'), the brand (human-readable issuer with state suffix, e.g. 'State Medicaid Agency â€” AK'), the state, and the raw_value (the original identifier the issuer assigned). When insurance[] is empty the Insurance section is still labeled but shows an empty list â€” no fallback prose. The raw other_identifiers[] array is internal â€” not shown to the user.

requirement.name: External research links always rendered
requirement.requirement: Every render MUST include Healthgrades (search by name + state) and the NPI Registry (lookup by NPI). The panel MUST also render a third link to the appropriate state medical board for the provider's primary practice state, with coverage for every US state and the District of Columbia. For practice addresses in US territories and outlying sovereignties (PR, GU, VI, AS, MP, etc.) the panel MUST render the licensing authority link appropriate to that sovereignty. Each link MUST prefill suitable search criteria (provider name, license number, NPI) where the destination supports it so the user lands already scoped to the right provider. Each link carries a short guidance string explaining what the user will find at the destination.

requirement.name: Page invocation contract
requirement.requirement: The panel MUST be invoked exclusively by the user clicking a Provider link. No utterance, no language-model call. The click payload carries the NPI and the link-as-shown snapshot (name, state, taxonomy) so the backend has the bare minimum to identify the record and run the data-management flow.

requirement.name: Rendering layer separation
requirement.requirement: The panel HTML template lives at Website/index.html (the host page). The FindCare iframe MUST send only structured data via a postMessage event carrying the provider record + the research-sites object. The host page owns the layout; the iframe owns the payload. No prose strings cross the postMessage boundary.

story.name: Provider Detail data management and retrieval
story.description: Every Provider Detail click triggers a four-step data-management cycle: (1) fetch the live NPPES record by NPI; (2) compare every NPPES-sourced field on the live response to the corresponding field on the provider record in our Mongo; (3) when divergence is detected, write the live values back into the provider record while preserving or re-running pipeline enrichments according to the per-enrichment rules below; (4) display proceeds from the current provider record via the display story. Our trust model is unchanged: NPPES is authoritative for NPPES-sourced fields; our pipeline owns the enrichments (county info, urban marker, can_prescribe, is_homeopathic, is_disqualified, active log, normalized licenses[], normalized insurance[], embedding). Insurance is sourced exclusively from NPPES other_identifiers and then normalized; there is no separate insurance feed.

requirement.name: Live NPPES fetch on every click
requirement.requirement: Every Provider Detail request MUST fetch the full NPI record from the NPPES Registry public API at https://npiregistry.cms.hhs.gov/api/?number={npi}&version=2.1 with a 10-second timeout. NPPES is the authoritative source for all NPPES-sourced fields: basic identity, taxonomies, addresses, other_identifiers, status, and enumeration date.

requirement.name: Compare live vs the provider record before writing
requirement.requirement: After the live fetch the backend MUST compare every NPPES-sourced field on the response to the corresponding field on the provider record. The comparison covers name, taxonomies (codes + primary switch), the full addresses array (line1, line2, city, state, ZIP, country, phone, address_type), the raw other_identifiers array, status, enumeration date, and active log. When every field matches, no write occurs and the flow proceeds directly to display.

requirement.name: Write-back on divergence
requirement.requirement: When the comparison detects any divergence the backend MUST overwrite the NPPES-sourced fields on the provider record with the live values, then re-run or preserve pipeline enrichments per the rules in REQ-B-005 through REQ-B-011. The write is a single document update; the display read happens after the write succeeds.

requirement.name: New-address county lookup via Google Maps only
requirement.requirement: When the live NPPES response includes an address NOT present on the provider record (a brand-new street + city + state), the backend MUST resolve the new address's county.fips and county.name by calling the Google Maps geocoding API exclusively. The pipeline's earlier-stage funnel (ZIP crosswalk, Census Geocoder, NPPES API) is NOT used in this path. The county.source on the new address MUST be stamped 'geocoder_pass4_maps' to record the resolution provenance. If Google does not return an authoritative result for the new address, the county object on that address MUST be omitted (the address ships without county info) and a WARNING MUST be logged naming the NPI and the unresolved address.

requirement.name: Urban marker left off on new addresses
requirement.requirement: When a new address is written back, county.urban MUST be left absent on the new address's county object. The urban marker is owned by the pipeline's USDA Rural-Urban Continuum Codes (RUCC) workbook pass and is re-stamped on the next full pipeline load. Until then the display story renders the new address with county name but no urban marker (per S-001-REQ-B-005).

requirement.name: Preserve county info on unchanged addresses
requirement.requirement: For every address on the live NPPES response that matches an existing address on the provider record, the backend MUST preserve the existing county object verbatim (county.fips, county.name, county.source, county.zip_ratio if present, county.urban if present). The county info is not re-computed; the prior pipeline run already paid the resolution cost and the inputs have not changed.

requirement.name: Re-run prescriber and homeopathic flags on taxonomy change
requirement.requirement: When the live NPPES taxonomies array differs from the provider record (any added, removed, or changed taxonomy code), the backend MUST recompute can_prescribe, is_homeopathic, and is_disqualified by ORing/ANDing across the new taxonomy set against the ProprietaryData.SpecialtyAndProviderFlags catalog (the same logic the pipeline's provider_flags_enrichment uses). When taxonomies are unchanged, these top-level flags MUST be preserved as-is.

requirement.name: Re-normalize licenses[] and insurance[] on write-back
requirement.requirement: On every write-back, the backend MUST replace BOTH the raw other_identifiers[] array (the NPPES-sourced data, exactly as the pipeline's normalize_provider_rows produces it) AND the normalized insurance[] array (the pipeline-derived form with insurance_type, brand, state, raw_value that the display consumes). Similarly the normalized licenses[] array MUST be regenerated from the live taxonomies' license fields so display and search consumers see consistent data. There is no enrichment of other_identifiers from any external insurance feed â€” NPPES is the only source.

requirement.name: Update active log if NPPES status changed
requirement.requirement: When the live NPPES basic.status, npi_deactivation_date, or npi_reactivation_date differs from the values represented by the last active[] log entry on the provider record, the backend MUST append a new event entry to active[] carrying the new event type (deactivated/reactivated), the date, the resulting is_active bool, and a source marker (nppes_deactivation_date / nppes_reactivation_date). When the status is unchanged, active[] is preserved verbatim.

requirement.name: Recompute quality flags after write-back
requirement.requirement: After write-back the backend MUST recompute the bad_data and out_of_scope flags from the new record state, using the same rules the pipeline's _mark_quality uses: bad_data {flagged: true, reason: 'no_address'} if addresses[] is empty; out_of_scope {flagged: true, reason: 'foreign_provider'} if the primary practice address country != 'US'; out_of_scope {flagged: true, reason: 'deactivated'} if the last active event is is_active=false. When inputs are unchanged the flags are preserved.

requirement.name: Stamp the provenance object on every successful write-back
requirement.requirement: On every successful write-back, the backend MUST set the provider record's sidecar provenance object as follows: provenance.origin = 'real_time_sync'; provenance.last_touched_at = the ISO timestamp of the write moment; provenance.real_time_sync_count is incremented by 1 if the field exists, otherwise initialized to 1. The four existing batch-ingest identifiers â€” load_id, loaded_at, chunk_id, row_index_in_chunk â€” MUST be preserved unchanged; they continue to identify the record's original pipeline ingest and are NEVER overwritten by a live write-back. The embedding, embedding_model, and embedding_version fields MUST also be preserved here; they are then superseded by REQ-B-014 when re-embedding completes.

requirement.name: Failure modes do not corrupt the record
requirement.requirement: When the NPPES live fetch fails (timeout, non-200, malformed response, zero results) OR the Google Maps geocoding call fails for a new address (covered separately by REQ-B-004), the backend MUST NOT write to the provider record. The display story is served from the existing (possibly stale) record. The failure is logged at WARNING. The user is not told the freshness sync failed â€” they see what we have.

requirement.name: One write per click, atomic, idempotent
requirement.requirement: When divergence is detected, the backend MUST issue exactly one MongoDB update against the provider record containing all the NPPES-sourced field updates plus the recomputed enrichment fields. Concurrent clicks for the same NPI MUST be safe â€” idempotent: the second write sees the same live response and either no-ops (because the first already wrote it) or produces identical fields.

requirement.name: Re-embed using the global embedding model on write-back
requirement.requirement: After a successful write-back, the backend MUST re-embed the record using the canonical global embedding model (per EPIC-008-F-011-S-004 and EPIC-002-F-005-S-012). The new embedding REPLACES the prior embedding, embedding_model, and embedding_version fields on the record. This keeps vector-search surfaces (provider search, specialty filter) consistent with the fresh field state after a live sync. If the embedding call fails, the prior embedding fields MUST be preserved and the write-back is still considered successful (the rest of the record is fresh; vector search will lag by one click until the next embedding attempt succeeds).

feature.name: Manage Front End Specialty Filter List
feature.description: Filter search results by specialty type, prescriber status, and homeopathic status. The term 'Homeopathic' in this feature refers to a Homeopathic provider â€” it is not a new classification and is not an umbrella label for the broader CAM/holistic/integrative-medicine set. Six-story decomposition: Display Specification, Present Initial Filter, User Manages Filter, User Submits Filter, API Surface and Contracts, Test Coverage.

story.description: How the SpecialtyFilter LOOKS and behaves end-to-end as a panel. Anchors the comprehensive UX description that S-002, S-003, and S-004 reference.

requirement.requirement:
The header uses a light green background. {find actual coded RGB value, or the term the CSS style sheet uses}
It is divided into three rows: a title row, a 'count' row, and a 'controls' row.
The title row says 'Choose Specialties'.
The Count row has 3 values where the label for each value is over the actual value. From left to right, the three values are:
"All possible": composed of the count of all the specialty types that can give care to the user based on the question they asked. This is regardless of whether or not a provider is available within the geographic boundary established by the user's question. In this group a specialty type must have a license but might not be homeopathic, or be able to prescribe.
"All prescribers": the total number of specialty types from 'All possible' that are legally allowed to write prescriptions. This includes, for example, Nurse Practitioners, and is not limited to physicians.
"Your choices": all the specialty types that the user has chosen. They might for example click the uncheck button and then check three specialties; in that case the number would be 3.
Macro Controls
The third row has three controls: a button 'Uncheck all' and two checkboxes 'Prescribers' and 'Homeopathic'. The two checkboxes are stacked vertically whereas the Uncheck button takes up the entire vertical space in this row. The controls in this header row do NOT determine what is submitted when Apply Filter is clicked â€” the only criterion for what gets submitted is the list of checked specialties. The header controls affect that checked-list state, but their purpose is to control which specialties are checked or presented; they are not intended to control what is done when Apply Filter is applied. The behavior of these controls is:
Uncheck All
"Uncheck all": this button unchecks any specialty type that is checked. Each time it is clicked it does this. If there are no specialties checked this button is greyed out, and a tool tip says, 'No specialties are checked'.
Additional requirement
When fewer than 50% of the rows are unchecked, the button's label reads 'Check All'. When it is in this state, the action is to check all specialties.
Prescribers
The list of checked specialists will have a particular state prior to the user clicking the Prescribers checkbox.
For all prescribers, Homeopathic and others, if the checkbox is unchecked it gets checked. If it is checked it remains checked.
For all non-prescribers, Homeopathic and non-Homeopath, if their checkbox is unchecked or checked, after this box is checked, the box becomes unchecked.
Homeopathic
The list of checked specialists will have a particular state prior to the user clicking the 'Homeopathic' checkbox.
For all Homeopathic specialties that treat this disorder specifically, if their checkbox is unchecked it gets checked. If it is checked it remains checked.
For all non-Homeopathic, prescribers or non-prescribers, if their checkbox is unchecked or checked, after this box is checked, the box becomes unchecked.
Additional behavior:
The result set returned to this list upon initialization will have two lists.
List one includes Homeopath specialties that specifically treat the class of problem that the user presented to the engine.
List two includes all homeopathic specialties in this area or generalists that can treat this type of problem. The server will try to eliminate non-logical choices such as midwives to treat erectile dysfunction or gerontologists to treat a child.
From a UX perspective there is only one list.
Scrollbar behavior
If there are more than 10 (configurable) then they are in a scroll bar, but all are available if the user scrolls.
Each specialty has on its right a checkbox. By default, all are checked. A user can check or uncheck any specialty. And they can click the Uncheck all button to remove all from being checked. This is going to be a typical behavior; user unchecks all and then checks some.
"Apply Filter" button: at the bottom of the control is a button labeled 'Apply Filter'. The scope of what gets applied is the specific specialties that are checked from the list of specialties. What is done with the controls in the header is not relevant to what specialties are submitted. Their purpose is to control which are checked or presented. They are not intended to control what is done when Apply Filter is applied. If any changes to the list of checked specialties have been made, then when this button is clicked:
A list of providers (the default list) will be in the center panel. Below that, potentially some providers might have been selected.
The provider list subject to selection but not selected shall be turned 'white' i.e. no records shall show.
A timer identical to the one that accompanied the original search shall be presented.
The selected provider window shall remain as is.
The prompt shall be available to the user.
The timer next to the prompt shall also show.
Middle-screen behavior on Apply Filter (per Skip clarification on the 'default list' / preservation question): the entire middle screen MUST be preserved as is from a business perspective. Specifically: the user's question is repainted; the Available Provider list is repainted; the Selected-for-evaluation panel never went away; the Prompt and 'send' never went away. Fine-grained technical requirements may be crafted from this baseline.
Timers (per Skip clarification): there are two timers. One timer is shown immediately to the LEFT of the user-prompt input box. The second timer is on the main screen. The main-screen timer is correct on Apply Filter except that the user's selected providers panel must be preserved (per the middle-screen-behavior clarification above). The prompt-adjacent timer is correct as is.
If no changes to the filter have been made (changes meaning new checks have been made) then the button will not be hot but greyed out, and if a user clicks the button a non-modal popup with an 'OK' button must say: 'There are no changes to apply, try a new prompt if this is the wrong list. The AI agent will help you craft the right question' and no other action will be taken.
Cache Results on client: in order to enhance performance and in contradiction to the general requirement that all business logic must be done in ChatHealthy's servers in the data center, the list of specialists MUST be cached on the client. Each time a new list of specialists is produced by the FindCare server the entire cache content must be replaced with the new list of specialties.
