story.name: Clinical Trial Detail display
story.description: The centre and right panels for one trial: the section anchors that lay the trial out, and the right-panel section list that jumps between them.

requirement.name: Center-panel trial detail: section anchors
requirement.requirement: Every section in the main-window trial detail MUST carry a stable anchor id of the form id="ct-sec-<slug>" where <slug> is a lowercased hyphenated form of the section title. The anchors are the targets for right-panel section-list jump links (REQ-B-070).

requirement.name: Right-panel section-list with smooth-scroll jumps
requirement.requirement: When a trial is displayed in the main window, the right panel MUST render a 'Trial sections' list with one clickable link per section in the current trial (linked to the anchor ids from REQ-B-069). Clicking a link MUST smooth-scroll the main-window center to that section's anchor.

requirement.name: Immediate clear + timer on More / Back click
requirement.requirement: When the user clicks More or Back in the left panel, the system MUST immediately (before the network round-trip): clear the main-window trial detail, clear the right-panel section list, start a one-second-tick timer from zero, and render a loading banner. Then the network fetch is issued. The user must never see stale data while a new page is being fetched.

requirement.name: Selected trial highlighted in left panel; click clears center+right immediately, then paints new trial
requirement.requirement: In the left-panel trial list, the trial currently displayed in frame_MainWindow MUST be visually distinguished (highlighted background) so the user always knows which card they are viewing. When the user clicks any trial card, the system MUST IMMEDIATELY blank frame_MainWindow and frame_RightPanel (paint empty content) BEFORE painting the new trial, so the user has an unambiguous visual confirmation that the click registered even when the new trial is fetched from the same in-memory page (no backend hop). The new trial's full detail is then painted into frame_MainWindow and its section-list into frame_RightPanel, and the left-panel highlight moves to the newly-selected card.

feature.name: Manage Front End Clinical Trial List
feature.description: Find recruiting clinical trials by condition. Decomposed into three stories (data retrieval, display, architecture). Stories and requirements pending operator approval of V5 draft in _oneshots/EPIC-006-F-005_FindClinicalTrials_FeatureDraft_V5.docx.

story.name: Find Clinical Trials data retrieval
story.description: ClinicalTrialsTool data-retrieval contract: CT.gov v2 search parameters, the geographic_scope filter (international or US-only), pagination defaults, demographic filters (age, sex), the canonical search_context echo, and the deterministic /gate op for pagination.

requirement.name: Request totalCount from CT.gov and surface the total to callers
requirement.requirement: ClinicalTrialsTool MUST send countTotal=true on every CT.gov v2 /studies request and parse payload.totalCount from the response. The total MUST be surfaced on Response.total_count for downstream display. CT.gov returns totalCount as an integer when countTotal=true.

requirement.name: Default page size of 10 records
requirement.requirement: Request.page_size MUST default to 10 (down from 25). The user explicitly paginates with the cursor returned in Response.cursor; the wrapper's pagination control mirrors the providers pagination pattern.

requirement.name: Accept optional participant demographics (age, sex)
requirement.requirement: Request MUST accept two optional participant-demographic fields: age_years (Optional[int]) and sex (Optional[str]). Condition remains the only required field. When age_years is supplied, ClinicalTrialsTool MUST map to CT.gov aggFilters using the canonical buckets: age<18 -> ages:child, 18<=age<65 -> ages:adult, age>=65 -> ages:older. When sex is supplied, ClinicalTrialsTool MUST resolve it to 'm' or 'f' (per S-003-REQ-B-007) and map to CT.gov sex:m or sex:f. Gender is intentionally NOT a parameter on this tool -- sex alone drives the CT.gov filter.

requirement.name: Always emit a 'trials' stream event on every code path
requirement.requirement: ClinicalTrialsTool MUST emit a {kind:'trials', data:Response} stream event on every code path -- success, empty result set, error. The client relies on the trials event as the canonical end-of-search signal; silent paths previously caused 'no trials event in stream' user-visible failures.

requirement.name: Echo authoritative SearchContext on every Response
requirement.requirement: ClinicalTrialsTool MUST populate Response.search_context with the exact {condition, user_location, age_years, sex, geographic_scope} actually used to fetch this page. The client uses search_context to re-issue pagination requests against the same canonical criteria, preventing the raw user utterance from leaking into the CT.gov call on subsequent pages.

requirement.name: Routes API failures must be surfaced (no silent swallow)
requirement.requirement: When the Google Routes API call for a destination fails, the tool MUST log the failure as a Mode 2 ChatHealthyException in one of four named modes: routes_api_key_missing (GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY env var absent), routes_api_non_200 (HTTP response not 200), routes_api_empty (200 with empty routes[]), and routes_api_failed (exception during the call). Distance/duration MAY remain absent on the affected Location; the operator is notified via the log.

requirement.name: Direct deterministic pagination op on /gate
requirement.requirement: SharedServices /gate MUST accept op='clinical_trials_page' with a payload matching ClinicalTrialsTool.Request (condition, user_location, age_years, sex, geographic_scope, cursor, page_size). UR dispatches to ClinicalTrialsTool with no LLM and no UtteranceManager hop. This is the deterministic path the client uses for More / Back pagination clicks (REQ-B-068).

requirement.name: Geographic scope: international (default) or US-only
requirement.requirement: Request MUST accept an optional geographic_scope field with values 'international' (default) or 'us'. ClinicalTrialsTool MUST honor it as follows: 'international' applies NO geographic filter to CT.gov (all records returned worldwide). 'us' MUST add the CT.gov v2 GEO filter restricting to country=United States. No other per-country scoping is supported in this iteration -- the only choices are international or US.

story.name: Clinical Trial List display
story.description: The left panel and the paging around it: the header band, the truncated summary, More/Back, the loading banner, and the error overlay. Selecting a trial belongs here; painting it belongs to Clinical Trial Detail.

requirement.name: Left-panel brief_summary truncated to first sentence with ellipsis
requirement.requirement: In the per-trial card in the left panel, the trial's brief_summary MUST be displayed truncated to its first sentence. When truncation occurs (the first sentence is shorter than the full summary), '...' MUST be appended to signal truncation. The user clicks the trial's NCT id to view the full detail in the main window.

requirement.name: Left-panel header band: canonical query criteria + record range
requirement.requirement: The colored header band at the top of the left panel MUST display the canonical query criteria as echoed by the tool (Response.search_context). Format: 'Clinical trials -- condition: <X>, subject age: <Y>, subject sex: <Z>, <location>, scope: <international|US>'. When the tool returns a total_count, the band MUST also append ' -- showing <start> to <end> of <total>'. When total is unknown the band MUST NOT show a count (it MUST NOT imply a count it does not know).

requirement.name: Left-panel More / Back pagination controls
requirement.requirement: The left panel MUST render a 'more trials' link when Response.cursor is non-null and a 'back' link when prior cursors exist (client-side history). Clicking either MUST round-trip through ClientRouter.getStreamedPayloads to /gate op='clinical_trials_page' (REQ-B-073) -- NOT through the LLM-routed utterance path. The pagination control mirrors the providers pagination pattern.

requirement.name: Loading banner content: canonical criteria + record range
requirement.requirement: The loading banner MUST display the canonical criteria (REQ-B-067 format, INCLUDING the geographic_scope) plus the record range being retrieved, e.g. 'condition: hepatitis B, subject age: 28, subject sex: male, Los Angeles, scope: US -- retrieving records 11-20 of 247'. The banner MUST NOT show only the raw user verb. The timer ticks every second next to or under the banner.

requirement.name: Mid-stream loading-banner update from intent_classified
requirement.requirement: On a fresh utterance flow, when UR has finished classifying the utterance into a findClinicalTrials intent, UR MUST emit a {kind:'intent_classified'} stream event carrying the canonical criteria (action, condition, user_location, age_years, sex, geographic_scope). The client MUST replace the loading banner's raw utterance text with the canonical criteria as soon as that event arrives, so the user sees what the system actually understood, not the raw utterance.

requirement.name: Pagination error overlay must include verb context
requirement.requirement: When a More / Back pagination fetch fails, the client error overlay MUST prepend a verb-context clause to the underlying error message: 'While trying to load more clinical trials: <err>' (for next) or 'While trying to go back to the previous page of clinical trials: <err>' (for prev). The user must always see what action was in flight when the error occurred.

story.name: Find Clinical Trials architecture
story.description: Architecture contract between UtteranceManager, Universal Router, and ClinicalTrialsTool. UM prompts for refinements on first turn and extracts on follow-up; LLM (not regex) resolves the sex answer; condition is the only required field; UR thin pass-through for the deterministic pagination op.

requirement.name: UtteranceManager prompts for refinements on first clinical-trial turn
requirement.requirement: On the FIRST turn where the user expresses clinical-trial interest, UM MUST set target_action='closeConnection200' and emit a user_message that names EVERY refinement field not already known. The literal words 'age', 'sex', 'location', and 'scope' (asking international vs US) MUST appear in the user_message for each field that is missing. UM MUST tell the user that condition alone is enough -- they can answer 'skip' for any field. Park a pending_disambiguation with kind='clinical_trial_demographics'. UM MAY skip the ask and dispatch findClinicalTrials directly ONLY when all refinements are already known.

requirement.name: UtteranceManager extracts age_years, sex, user_location, geographic_scope from follow-up
requirement.requirement: On the FOLLOW-UP turn after the prompt, UM MUST extract every refinement supplied. age_years (int) from 'I'm 28' / '28' / '28yo' / 'age 28'. sex (lowercased 'm' or 'f') per REQ-B-007. user_location (free-text) from any location mention. geographic_scope ('international' or 'us') from any 'international'/'worldwide'/'US only'/'United States only' mention. Populate all extracted fields as Arguments on the findClinicalTrials intent. If the user declines ('skip', 'no', 'just show me'), proceed with whatever fields are populated. Always set target_action='findClinicalTrials'.

requirement.name: LLM-driven resolution of the user's sex answer to 'm' or 'f'
requirement.requirement: UM MUST resolve the user's answer to the sex prompt — or any sex signal in a free-text utterance — into the canonical lowercase token 'm' or 'f' via the classifier LLM. The LLM, not regex, MUST be authoritative. The LLM MUST recognize: (a) direct labels — 'Male', 'M', 'man', 'boy', 'masculino' → 'm'; 'Female', 'F', 'woman', 'girl' → 'f'; (b) male family / relationship words referring to the subject — 'son', 'brother', 'father', 'dad', 'uncle', 'nephew', 'grandfather', 'grandpa', 'husband', 'boyfriend', 'fiancé' → 'm'; (c) female family / relationship words — 'daughter', 'sister', 'mother', 'mom', 'aunt', 'niece', 'grandmother', 'grandma', 'wife', 'girlfriend', 'fiancée' → 'f'; (d) third-person pronouns about the subject when no contradicting label is present — 'he', 'his', 'him' → 'm'; 'she', 'her', 'hers' → 'f'. If the answer is ambiguous, non-binary, or mixes signals the LLM cannot reconcile, sex MUST be left None and the search dispatches without a sex filter. Gender is not a parameter in this iteration; we ask sex only. The same rules apply BOTH on the dedicated follow-up prompt AND on the first turn when the user volunteers the information ('clinical trial for my son who is 9' → sex='m', age_years=9).

requirement.name: Condition is the ONLY required field for findClinicalTrials

feature.description:
This feature specifies the rules that must be enforced by the chatHealthy.ai dev ops infrastructure utilizing the Anthopic Hooks as event triggers. 
It specifies the concrete DevOps surface that wires Claude Code's hook architecture into ChatHealthy governance. Hosts SessionStart / PostCompact / UserPromptSubmit / Stop enforcement entries declared in engineering_rules.json, the chathealthy_devops_boot program (Rule-002), and the conversation-log persistence path (Rule-001). Owns the operator-visible boot lifecycle: conversation context replay and agile_backlog taxonomy injection on both new-session begin and post-compaction restart.

story.name: Rules infrastructure: manager, base worker, lock, timeout, telemetry, exit-code aggregation
story.description: ChatHealthyEnforcementManager + EnforcementWorker (abstract base) deliver the framework: read-only rules-registry load, hook-filtered enforcement dispatch, manager-owned mutex coordination, per-worker subprocess timeout, structured violation/telemetry envelopes, and worst-code-wins aggregation. Per V20 Â§4.4. The manager is invoked by every Git and Claude Code hook with a single hook_name argument.

requirement.name: Rules carry enforcement entries
requirement.requirement: Every engineering rule that the team intends to enforce MUST carry at least one programmatic enforcement entry. A rule with an empty enforcement array is documentation, not governance, and SHALL be either populated, retired, or annotated as documentation-only.

requirement.name: Enforcement at hook moment
requirement.requirement: Enforcement runs at the moment a violation can occur â€” the relevant Git or Claude Code hook â€” not on a separate cadence. There is no nightly job that catches yesterday's mistake.

requirement.name: Hook-agnostic framework
requirement.requirement: An engineering rule MUST be able to attach to any of the four Git hooks (pre-commit, commit-msg, post-commit, pre-push) and any of the six Claude Code hooks (SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse, Stop, SessionEnd, InstructionsLoaded). The framework is hook-agnostic; the enforcement entry declares its hook.

requirement.name: Human debuggability
requirement.requirement: The system MUST be debuggable by a human. One file per role. One class per file. One entry point. Per-enforcement, per-worker structured stdout and telemetry, with worst exit code propagated.

requirement.name: Multi-PID concurrency
requirement.requirement: The framework MUST handle multi-PID race conditions correctly. The same hook can fire many times concurrently across different Claude Code PIDs and Git invocations. The manager acquires a lock before dispatching any worker whose enforcement entry declares requires_lock = True; in-process locks are forbidden.

requirement.name: Additive enforcement
requirement.requirement: Adding the next enforcement MUST be a small, additive change. New enforcement entries get a new enforcement_id and â€” if needed â€” a new worker subclass; existing rules and workers are not touched.

requirement.name: Worker inherits base class
requirement.requirement: Every worker MUST inherit from EnforcementWorker. Subclasses implement only their domain-specific check logic. The base class owns scope evaluation, violation shape, exit codes, telemetry, and error handling so every worker behaves the same from the manager's perspective.

requirement.name: Enforcement entry first-class
requirement.requirement: Enforcement entries are first-class records: every entry carries a stable enforcement_id (format <rule_id>-ENF-NNN), a declared hook, an executable_path, a scopes field carrying scope-list rules in the four canonical types (allowed_exact, allowed_pattern, excluded_exact, excluded_pattern), and a requires_lock boolean. They can be cited in audit trails, bug reports, and the backlog like requirements are today.

requirement.name: Filesystem mirrors operating model
requirement.requirement: The architecture MUST be aligned with the EPIC / Feature / Story tree. Filesystem mirrors operating model. The home for this feature is projectRoot/architecture/EngineeringRuleEnforcement/. crossEpicConcerns/ holds shared business artifacts only â€” no code lives there.

requirement.name: V1 demonstrability

requirement.name: Four canonical scope-list types

story.name: Rule-003 - Deliberate raises must use ChatHealthyException
story.description: Establishes the foundational rule and the implementation that realizes it. Defines ChatHealthyException in chathealthy-lib, specifies the constructor contract (mode discriminator + message for logging + context dict), mandates the substitution at every existing deliberate-raise site in our authored code, and adds a pre-commit gate that rejects new raises of forbidden built-in exception types in our modules. The first mode the substrate uses is llm_unavailable, introduced by the LLM facade with context {provider, call_site, attempts}. Additional modes (compliance violations, geography insufficient, db unreachable, rate limited, etc.) land as the operator approves their definitions; the substrate accepts them without code change at the catch sites.

requirement.name: ChatHealthyException class definition
requirement.requirement: The chathealthy-lib package MUST define a class ChatHealthyException that inherits from the standard library Exception. The constructor signature is (mode: str, message: str, **context). Message is used for logging, and not for end user communications. Context is a dict; its keys vary by mode. The instance exposes attributes mode (str), message (str), context (dict), and exception (Exception â€” the original wrapped exception, when ChatHealthyException is being raised as a boundary conversion of an external library exception; None when this is an originating raise from our own code). The class lives at a stable import path within the package so every consumer service can import it.

requirement.name: Exhaustive use rule for deliberate raises in our authored code
requirement.requirement: Every deliberate raise of an exception authored in ChatHealthy.ai repository code MUST use ChatHealthyException with an appropriate mode discriminator. Use of built-in Python exception types (ValueError, RuntimeError, AssertionError, TypeError, KeyError) in deliberate raises authored by our code is forbidden. Re-raises of external exceptions (e.g. httpx.RemoteProtocolError, pymongo.errors.*) preserve the original type and the call stack of the original exception, so that logging of the exception becomes the duty of the exception class and not the code that creates the exception.

requirement.name: Boundary conversion rule for external-library exceptions
requirement.requirement: External-library exceptions MAY be converted to ChatHealthyException at defined system boundaries. The LLM facade (EPIC-008-F-002-S-009-REQ-B-007 below) is one such boundary. When such a conversion happens, the exception object MUST log the original exception with full traceback for operator forensic value before raising the new ChatHealthyException, so the original failure is not lost.

requirement.name: Catch-side discrimination on mode
requirement.requirement: Code that catches ChatHealthyException SHOULD discriminate on the mode attribute, not on isinstance against new exception subclasses (there are no subclasses). The mode taxonomy is the design surface for discriminating failure shapes. Catch sites that need to handle several modes use an explicit conditional on exc.mode.

requirement.name: Mode taxonomy lives in the feature's design doc
requirement.requirement: The set of valid modes is documented in the feature's architecture design doc under ChatHealthyLib/architectureAndDesign/. Adding a new mode is a design-doc edit that the operator approves, not a code-only change. Code that raises with an undocumented mode MAY be rejected by a future enforcement gate (out of scope for this story).

requirement.name: Pre-commit gate forbids deliberate raises of built-in types
requirement.requirement: A new engineering rule (Rule-NNN, operator picks the number) MUST gate pre-commit. The worker scans every staged Python file under ChatHealthy.ai's authored directories (sharedServices/, FindCare/, evaluateCare/, Code/, ChatHealthyLib/, architecture/) and rejects any line matching a deliberate raise of ValueError, RuntimeError, AssertionError, KeyError, TypeError. Exempted: re-raises with no expression, test files asserting expected behavior, and external-library calls that we do not author. Any violation found — new or legacy — is rejected. No carve-outs for historical code.

requirement.name: LLM facade boundary defines the first concrete mode llm_unavailable
requirement.requirement: The LLM call facade in chathealthy-lib catches transient HTTP errors (httpx.RemoteProtocolError, httpx.ConnectError, httpx.ReadTimeout, httpx.WriteTimeout, httpx.PoolTimeout) from the underlying pydantic-ai Agent.run call and, after the retry policy is exhausted, raises ChatHealthyException(mode='llm_unavailable', provider=<str>, call_site=<str>, attempts=<int>). UR catches this exception in _handle_utterance and re-dispatches to UM as a manufacture-trigger Request whose manufacture_utterance_reason carries the same context, so UM authors a user-facing message via the existing manufacture pattern. If the manufacture call itself raises ChatHealthyException, that exception propagates to UR's outermost catch and the existing fatal path fires; the operator sees the failure via telemetry and the user sees chFatalError. This three-rung ladder (transient blip covered by retry, sustained-recoverable covered by manufacture dialogue, truly-down covered by fatal) is the substrate.

requirement.name: Exception Management Modes
requirement.requirement: Every catch site that catches a ChatHealthyException MUST classify the caught exception into exactly one of three modes and act accordingly. Mode 1 â€” expected and easily handled (retry, fallback, alternate path): catcher logs at INFO with the if_debug flag set so the record is emitted only when in debug; caller continues via the recovery mechanism; user sees nothing. Mode 2 â€” expected and probably attributable to user error OR to a resource temporarily unavailable: catcher logs at ERROR (always emitted, no debug gate), surfaces an appropriate user-facing message describing the problem, and does NOT return HTTP 503. Mode 3 â€” unhandled, NOT expected (a bug): the safety-net @app.exception_handler returns HTTP 503 to the user and logs the unhandled exception so we can track it down and fix it; Mode 3 is the ONLY case where the user sees an HTTP 503; the architectural goal is for Mode 3 occurrences to be RARE â€” every observed Mode 3 instance MUST become a local catch with Mode 1 or Mode 2 handling. Throw-side rule: when a catch site converts a library exception (httpx, pymongo, etc.) into a ChatHealthyException, that site MUST clean up the underlying resource (close the connection / cursor / file handle, abort the request, release the pool slot, etc.) before raising the ChatHealthyException, so a leaked resource does not produce a delayed second failure (e.g., a 100-second-later timeout from a connection that was never closed).

requirement.name: Explicit per-call batch_size override on library find()
requirement.requirement: The ChatHealthyMongoUtilities Mongo wrapper SHALL expose batch_size as an explicit named keyword parameter on its find() method, with default value None. When batch_size is None the library MUST NOT pass any batch_size to pymongo (pymongo default applies). When the caller sets batch_size to an integer, the library MUST forward that integer to pymongo. The library MUST NOT impose a default batch_size for any caller, MUST NOT cache or persist a batch_size across calls, and MUST NOT infer a batch_size from collection size or call history. Choosing to override batch_size is a per-call caller decision. The exception argument passed to ChatHealthyLoggingService log methods (exc_info=, or the implicit current exception captured by log.exception() inside an except block) MUST be a ChatHealthyException; passing a non-ChatHealthyException exception is forbidden.

requirement.name: Per-call debug gate - opt-in conditional emission
requirement.requirement: Every log call to a ChatHealthyLoggingService logger MUST accept an optional parameter (working name `if_not_debug_log` - final name TBD). requirement.name: No persistent-state change from React

requirement.name: No business logic outside tools

story.name: Commit
story.description: This story establishes the requirements for ChatHealthy.ai's commit management and governance. How code enters the repository: every commit is explicitly authorized by the operator at the moment it fires, lands on the dev branch and no other, and passes every engineering-rule scan across the whole repository before it is created. A commit that fails any scan is not made.

requirement.name: Every committed file is governed by the rule manager
requirement.requirement: There MUST be an engineering rule enforcing that any file committed to the ChatHealthy.ai repository is subject to governance by ChatHealthy's rule manager. No file reaches the repository without having been examined by the rule manager, and no file is exempt from examination except by an entry on a rule's exclusion list in engineering_rules.json.

story.name: Promote
story.description: This story establishes the requirements for ChatHealthy.ai's promotion management and governance. How a git baseline is established and advanced through the environment chain: a promote captures the entire working tree at one commit -- nothing stashed, excluded or hidden -- and advances only along the adjacent pairs local to dev, dev to qa, qa to prod, leaving the destination byte-identical to the source.

requirement.name: A promoted tree matches the tree it was promoted from
requirement.requirement: Each promote MUST result in the destination holding a tree identical to the tree of the source it was promoted from. For local to dev the source is the operator's working tree; for dev to qa it is the dev branch tip; for qa to prod it is the qa branch tip. A promote that cannot establish that the two trees are identical MUST fail and MUST NOT advance the destination.

requirement.name: A promote advances from one environment to the next: local -> dev -> qa -> prod
requirement.requirement: Local files promote to dev, dev promotes to qa, and qa promotes to production on the main branch.

requirement.name: No promotion outside the chain
requirement.requirement: Any promotion that is not one of the three pairs in the chain MUST be refused. This includes skipping an environment, promoting in reverse, and promoting an environment to itself.

requirement.name: No file may remain stashed when promoting
requirement.requirement: When promoting, no file may remain stashed. Any stash present MUST be applied into the working tree so the promote carries it; the promote does not proceed while work is parked in a stash.

requirement.name: One uncommittable file fails the whole promotion
requirement.requirement: If any file cannot be committed, the entire promotion MUST fail. A promote is all of the tree or none of it; no partial promotion is produced, and the destination is not advanced.

requirement.name: All promotions must be auditably approved by a human operator
requirement.requirement: Every code promotion MUST be approved by a human operator prior to any changes in the code REPO. This approval MUST be absolutely auditable, such that there is proof that a human and not an agent did the approval.

story.name: Build
story.description: This story establishes the requirements for ChatHealthy.ai's build management and governance. How source becomes a deployable package: a build reads the working tree for local and origin of the environment's branch for dev, qa and prod, and writes one directory per target per package. The operator names the targets and the packages; there is no build-everything shortcut.

requirement.name: Build data lives entirely in deployment_architecture.json
requirement.requirement: Build data MUST be 100% contained in deployment_architecture.json, and that file MUST have a strict schema. No build fact is held anywhere else -- not in build scripts, not in the build output, not in a second copy of the manifest. The schema MUST forbid undeclared properties, so a fact the schema does not describe cannot be introduced without the schema being changed first.

requirement.name: A target declares one set of files, packages, secrets and variables
requirement.requirement: A target MUST declare exactly one set of files, packages, secrets and variables, and that set MUST serve every environment the target is bound to. A second declaration of the same fact for a different environment is forbidden. Where a target's contents differ between two environments, that difference is a defect in the declaration and not a property of the target.

requirement.name: Only what genuinely varies by environment is declared per environment
requirement.requirement: An environment binding MUST declare only what genuinely differs between environments: which host runs the target, the address it answers on, and the vault or cluster it reads. It MUST NOT declare files, packages, secrets or variables. A target MAY declare a default for any per-environment fact, and an environment that declares nothing takes that default; a per-environment declaration MUST exist only where the value actually differs.

requirement.name: A package declares the packages it depends on
requirement.requirement: A package MUST declare every package it requires in order to function, by package_id. The resulting graph MUST be acyclic. A build MUST fail where a declared dependency does not exist, and where the graph contains a cycle. Install order MUST be derived from these declarations and MUST NOT be encoded in the build or deploy programs.

requirement.name: A build produces a digest that identifies each package's contents
requirement.requirement: Every package a build produces MUST carry a digest computed over the exact bytes of its declared contents, normalised for line endings. The digest MUST change when any declared content changes and MUST NOT change otherwise. The digest MUST be recorded in the build output so a deploy can compare what a host holds against what the build produced. Every deployed host MUST report, on request, the package_id and digest of every package it carries, so that the build running in a given environment on a given host can be established unequivocally from the host itself rather than inferred from a deploy record or a log.

requirement.name: Each build must be complete and start from a null base
requirement.requirement: Prior to each build, all builds MUST be destroyed. Only the packages named as parameters of the build invocation MUST be built. No fact from a pre-existing build may be used in a new one.

requirement.name: The record names no technology
requirement.requirement: deployment_architecture.json and the schema it validates against MUST NOT name a vendor, a platform, a product or a programming language. A platform-specific fact MUST be carried as a named platform holding an array of name/value facts, and a language-specific fact as a named language holding the same shape. The schema MUST validate the shape of a fact and MUST NOT enumerate which platforms or languages exist. The code that installs to a platform owns the knowledge of which facts that platform requires and MUST verify them; a platform the code does not support MUST fail the deploy naming the platform.

story.name: Deploy
story.description: This story establishes the requirements for ChatHealthy.ai's deployment management and governance. How a built package reaches its destination: a deploy reads only the build output, never source, and installs each named package to the target that declares it. The running target reports which build it carries, and the deploy verifies that rather than asserting it.

requirement.name: A deploy reads only build output
requirement.requirement: A deploy MUST read only what a build produced. It MUST NOT read the repository source tree, and MUST NOT construct, transform or substitute any artifact at deploy time. Where the build output does not contain something a target declares, the deploy MUST fail and report what was missing rather than obtain it from source.

requirement.name: Each named package installs to the target that declares it
requirement.requirement: A deploy names its targets and its packages, and installs each named package to the target whose declaration in deployment_architecture.json carries it. A package the named targets do not declare MUST NOT be installed. A target MUST receive only the packages it declares and that the operator named. Naming several targets in one invocation MUST deploy each of them.

requirement.name: A running target reports the build it carries
requirement.requirement: Every deployed target MUST report, on demand and without operator action, the build number and the commit its running code was produced from. A target that cannot say which build it carries MUST be treated as unverified.

requirement.name: The deploy verifies the build that arrived
requirement.requirement: After installing, a deploy MUST read back from the running target the build it reports, and compare it to the build that was installed. Agreement is the only evidence the deploy succeeded; a deploy MUST NOT report success on the basis of having sent the artifact. Disagreement, or an unreadable report, MUST fail the deploy for that target.

requirement.name: Deployment argument definition
requirement.requirement: A deploy invocation MUST accept exactly one environment, and MUST deploy to that environment and no other. It MUST accept an array of targets containing at least one target. For each named target it MUST accept an array of packages containing at least one package, so that every package named is bound to the target it is being deployed to. An invocation naming no target, naming a target with no packages, or naming more than one environment MUST be refused before anything is deployed.

requirement.name: Every deployment is approved by a human and the approval is recorded
requirement.requirement: Every deployment MUST be approved by a human operator before anything is deployed, and that approval MUST be recorded in the approvals repository. On completion the deployment MUST record its outcome -- success or failure -- in the approvals repository, referencing the approval that authorized it. A refusal to approve is not a failure of the deployment; it MUST be recorded in the approvals repository as a rejected deployment. Local deploys are exempt from this requirement. It is required that a local deploy can be accomplished by code bots without human intervention.

requirement.name: A deploy behaves identically in every environment
requirement.requirement: Each deployment MUST result in identical code, metadata, binaries, environment variables, and secrets in each environment. Where a deploy succeeds in one environment and fails in the next, the cause MUST be a difference in that environment's idiosyncratic ways of receiving a deployment, not a difference in the facts of the deployment.

requirement.name: The environment selects the host and nothing else
requirement.requirement: The host that runs a target MUST be a property of the environment binding, not of the target. An environment binding MUST select the host and MUST NOT alter what is deployed. The deploy MUST dispatch on the declared host only at the point of installation; no other step may vary by environment or by host.

requirement.name: Every declared secret is resolved by name in every environment
requirement.requirement: Every secret and variable a target declares MUST be resolved individually, by the name the declaration gives it, in every environment without exception. A deploy MUST NOT hand a target a store wholesale: no environment may receive a file, a vault, or any other collection of values in place of the named entries it declares. Where a declared name cannot be resolved from the store it is bound to, the deploy MUST fail, naming the entry, the store and the environment, and MUST NOT substitute a value from any other source or install the target partially.

requirement.name: Packages install in the order their dependencies require
requirement.requirement: A deploy MUST install packages in an order satisfying every declared dependency, and MUST derive that order from the declarations rather than from any order written into the program. Where a dependency fails to install, the packages depending on it MUST NOT be installed, and the deploy MUST fail reporting which dependency was not met.

requirement.name: A package is installed whole or not at all
requirement.requirement: A package MUST be installed in its entirety or not installed. A deploy MUST NOT install part of a package, and MUST NOT leave a host carrying a partially installed package. Where installation of any part of a package fails, the deploy MUST fail for that target and report the package that failed.

requirement.name: An unchanged package is verified identical rather than assumed present
requirement.requirement: A deploy MAY skip installing a package only after verifying that what the host holds is byte-for-byte identical to what the build produced, by comparing the digest the host reports against the digest recorded in the build output. The presence of a package by name MUST NOT be taken as evidence that it is current. Where the host cannot report a digest, the package MUST be installed.

requirement.name: A deploy can create every target it installs to from nothing
requirement.requirement: A deploy MUST be able to create every target it installs to where that target does not yet exist, including hosts, vaults, secrets, databases and their indexes, and identities. An environment MUST be reproducible end to end from the repository and the deploy alone, with no manual step. Where creating a target requires a privilege the deploying identity does not hold, the deploy MUST fail naming the privilege.

requirement.name: No secret that is not in deployment_architecture.json CAN exist on a host
requirement.requirement: Subsequent to a deploy, no secret that is not in deployment_architecture.json CAN exist on a host. Each deployment execution MUST ensure that no such secret exists, and MUST log all secrets that are removed as a part of the deployment.

feature.name: Conversation Archive
feature.description: Every operator utterance and every Claude response is recorded as business data in the conversation archive. Capture never delays the interaction and never loses an utterance because something downstream is unavailable, except as an extreme defence. Credentials, secrets and offensive language are removed before anything is archived. Content that never reaches the archive is not kept indefinitely, and the archive is re-examined as knowledge of credentials grows. Every utterance is classified so the archive can be reasoned about. The document shape is governed by https://dev.chathealthy.ai/schemas/ChatHealthyDevOpsUtteranceSchema.json

story.name: Capture utterances
story.description: Every operator utterance and every Claude response is captured and lands in the conversation archive, verbatim, correctly attributed, and carrying the time it was made. Capture must never make the operator wait and must never lose an utterance because something downstream is unavailable. Credentials must not reach the archive.

requirement.name: Operator is told when capture fails
requirement.requirement: If an utterance cannot be captured, the operator MUST be shown an unmistakable full-screen warning stating that the utterance was NOT recorded. Capture failure MUST NOT be silent.

requirement.name: Every utterance is recorded
requirement.requirement: Every operator utterance and every Claude response MUST be recorded in the conversation archive.

requirement.name: Capture does not delay the operator
requirement.requirement: Capturing an utterance MUST NOT delay the interaction. No work depending on a remote service may occur before the turn completes.

requirement.name: No utterance is lost while the archive is unreachable
requirement.requirement: No utterance MUST be lost while the conversation archive is unreachable. Captured content MUST be retained until the archive confirms it has been stored, except as an extreme defensive measure to protect disk space or other resources.

requirement.name: No credential, secret or offensive language is stored
requirement.requirement: No credential, secret or offensive language CAN be stored in the conversation archive.

requirement.name: Utterances are recorded verbatim
requirement.requirement: An utterance MUST be recorded exactly as it was made. It MUST NOT be summarised, paraphrased, answered, or replaced by any other text. Only the removal of a credential, secret or item of offensive language may alter it.

requirement.name: Utterances are correctly attributed
requirement.requirement: Every recorded utterance MUST be attributed to the party that made it. An utterance MUST NOT be attributed to the wrong party.

requirement.name: Utterances carry the time they were made
requirement.requirement: Every recorded utterance MUST carry the time the utterance was made, which MUST be distinguishable from the time it reached the archive.

requirement.name: Concurrent utterances are all recorded
requirement.requirement: Utterances made concurrently MUST all be recorded. No utterance may be lost, overwritten, or merged with another because two occurred at the same moment.

requirement.name: A removed credential is identified
requirement.requirement: Where a credential is removed from an utterance, the archive MUST identify which credential was removed by stipulating the key of the key/value pair associated with the credential or secret.

requirement.name: Offensive language is redacted
requirement.requirement: When the human operator swears, the curse word or words MUST be replaced with the phrase 'Expletive redacted'.

requirement.name: Every utterance carries the speaker role
requirement.requirement: Every recorded utterance MUST carry the speaker's part in the exchange, which MUST be distinct from the identity of the speaker.

requirement.name: Every human utterance identifies the person
requirement.requirement: Every recorded utterance made by a human MUST identify that person. The archive MUST support more than one person.

requirement.name: The time an utterance reached the archive is recorded
requirement.requirement: Every recorded utterance MUST carry the time it reached the archive, so that archiving latency is measurable.

story.name: Purge
story.description: Captured content that never reaches the archive is not kept indefinitely, its loss is visible, and the archive is re-examined against current knowledge of credentials so that a secret recorded before it was known does not remain.

requirement.name: Unarchived content is deleted after 24 hours
requirement.requirement: Captured content that has not reached the conversation archive within 24 hours MUST be deleted.

requirement.name: Archive is re-scrubbed against current credential knowledge
requirement.requirement: The conversation archive MUST be re-scrubbed against current knowledge of credentials, so that a credential recorded before it was known is removed once it is known.

requirement.name: Content still eligible for archiving is not deleted
requirement.requirement: Captured content that has not yet reached its deletion age MUST NOT be deleted, however many attempts to archive it have failed.

requirement.name: Deletion is recorded
requirement.requirement: When captured content is deleted before reaching the archive, the loss MUST be recorded so that it is known to have occurred and how much was lost.

story.name: Categorize
story.description: All utterances must be categorized with metadata.

requirement.name: Each utterance carries an orderable time
requirement.requirement: Each utterance MUST carry the time it was made in a form the database can index and order chronologically, so that ordering is correct across daylight-saving transitions.

requirement.name: Each utterance carries a human-readable time
requirement.requirement: Each utterance MUST carry its time rendered for reading, in Pacific time on a 12-hour clock. This rendering MUST NOT be used for ordering.

requirement.name: Each utterance speaker is identified
requirement.requirement: Each utterance is from some human user who MUST be identified, or from Claude Code.

requirement.name: Tone is classified
requirement.requirement: Every utterance MUST be classified by tone, using a value from the approved enumeration. No utterance MAY remain without a tone.

requirement.name: Utterance class is classified
requirement.requirement: Every utterance MUST be classified by what it was doing, using a value from the approved enumeration. No utterance MAY remain without an utterance class.

requirement.name: Classification values come from a normative schema
requirement.requirement: The permitted values for tone and utterance class MUST be defined in a normative JSON schema. A classification MUST NOT use a value absent from that schema.

requirement.name: The archive conforms to its schema
requirement.requirement: Every record in the conversation archive MUST validate against the normative schema that governs it.

feature.name: ChatHealthy PKI Certificate Management
feature.description: PKI certificate authority and lifecycle management for ChatHealthy.ai. Owns X.509 certificate issuance, key generation, subject naming, validity periods, storage/retrieval from Azure Key Vault, certificate tracking, and revocation handling. Integrates with identity and authentication subsystems to provide mTLS and mutual authentication infrastructure.

story.name: Certificate Management (umbrella story)
story.description: Umbrella story defining the complete certificate management lifecycle. Establishes the contract that all certificate operations MUST flow through this feature. Covers the decision tree for when to issue, renew, revoke, and retire certificates. Defines the canonical certificate naming authority and the versioning scheme for certificate generations. Establishes the audit trail requirements for all certificate lifecycle events.

story.name: Certificate Issuance - issue X.509 certs for services/clients
story.description: On-demand X.509 certificate issuance for ChatHealthy services, clients, and components. The issuance path accepts a certificate request (CSR or parameters), validates the request against policy (subject name, validity period, key usage), and returns a signed certificate and intermediate chain. Requests originate from service bootstrap (at deploy time), operator direct invocation, or automated renewal triggers. All issued certificates are tracked in the certificate registry.

story.name: Key Generation - generate RSA keypairs
story.description: RSA keypair generation as a prerequisite to certificate issuance. Generates 2048-bit or 4096-bit RSA keypairs depending on security posture requirements per environment. Private keys are generated in-memory, never written to disk in unencrypted form, and immediately enrolled with their paired certificate into the vault. Key generation is deterministic per environment and subject name to enable reproducibility.

story.name: Subject Naming - define how cert CNs are structured
story.description: Certificate subject naming policy. Defines the canonical structure for certificate common names (CNs), subject alternative names (SANs), and issuer names. CNs follow the pattern: <service-id>.<environment>.chathealthy.internal (e.g., findcare-backend.dev.chathealthy.internal). SANs include both DNS and IP forms for multi-homed services. Issuer CN follows: ChatHealthy CA <generation> <environment> (e.g., ChatHealthy CA 1 dev). Naming scheme is immutable once deployed; any change requires a new CA generation.

story.name: Validity Periods - 1 year validity
story.description: Certificate validity periods default to 1 year from issuance. All issued certificates MUST have NotBefore = issuance time and NotAfter = issuance time + 365 days. Certificates approaching expiration (within 30 days) trigger automated renewal via a scheduled job. Manual early renewal is operator-callable. Validity period is immutable once issued; certificates cannot be extended in place.

story.name: Vault Integration - store/retrieve certs from Key Vault
story.description: Azure Key Vault integration for certificate and private key storage. Issued certificates and their private keys are stored in Key Vault with metadata tagging (service_id, environment, generation, issuer_thumbprint). Retrieval is role-gated: only services with the appropriate RBAC role can retrieve their own certificate and key material. All vault operations are logged to the audit trail. Key Vault certificate versions are maintained automatically by Azure; ChatHealthy tracks generation IDs independently for cross-environment promotion.

story.name: Certificate Tracking - track all certificates
story.description: Certificate registry maintained in MongoDB collection ProprietaryData.CertificateRegistry. Every issued certificate is registered with: subject CN, SANs, issuer CN, thumbprint (SHA-1), thumbprint (SHA-256), public key hash, NotBefore, NotAfter, serial number, service_id, environment, generation, CA version, vault location, issuance timestamp, renewal trigger timestamp (if auto-renewed), revocation status. Registry is append-only: updates are new documents, never mutations. Queries against the registry provide the single source of truth for 'which certificates are live' and 'which are approaching expiration'. Registry is auditable and immutable by design.

story.name: Revocation - handle certificate revocation
story.description: Certificate revocation handling for compromised or obsolete certificates. Revocation is initiated by operator command and takes effect immediately: the certificate record in the registry is marked revoked, Key Vault secret is retired (no longer retrievable), and all downstream systems are notified via an audit event. Services holding a revoked certificate MUST detect the revocation on their next authentication check (via certificate pinning validation) and must not accept the certificate for further TLS handshakes. No CRL or OCSP responder is required; revocation state is determined by querying the registry at authentication time.

epic.name: Pipelines
epic.description: This epic defines all the requirements for ChatHealthy's data pipelines, which do data ETL and data quality management, and data enrichment. All of the code lives and executes in Azure and writes to the ChatHealthyDataPipelines cluster.

feature.name: Data Pipeline Infrastructure Requirements
feature.description: This feature specifies the requirements for ChatHealthy's data pipeline infrastructure. The purpose of the feature is to specify the common requirements allowing for data pipelines to be executed in the most possible cost effective manner, with robust reliability and observability.

story.name: A reaper component MUST manage the Pipeline Cluster's uptime
story.description: The pipeline cluster must not be running when nothing needs it.

requirement.name: A Reaper component external to any pipeline runs regularly
requirement.requirement: A component named Reaper MUST exist, MUST be external to every pipeline, and MUST run on a regular basis and at least once per hour, to realize these requirements and so guard against a failure in a pipeline job or an expired reservation made by an agent on behalf of itself or of a human user.

requirement.name: The reaper corrects pipeline job metadata a failed job left wrong
requirement.requirement: When a pipeline job fails to leave its own metadata true, the Reaper MUST correct it, so that no job is recorded in a non-terminal state while it is not running and no lock or reservation is held on behalf of a job that is not running.

requirement.name: An incomplete metadata correction says so
requirement.requirement: When the Reaper cannot complete a correction pass, the pipeline job metadata MUST record that the pass was incomplete and what it did not reach, and MUST be distinguishable from a pass that completed having found nothing to correct.

feature.name: Data Migration
feature.description: This feature specifies the requirements for ChatHealthy.ai's migration of published data from the pipeline cluster to the front-end cluster. A migration moves collections from ChatHealthyDataPipelines.PipelinePublicHealthData to ChatHealthyFrontEnd.PublicHealthData. A collection arrives under the name it left with. Nothing is transformed in transit. Migration is the only path by which data reaches the front-end cluster. It is separate from the pipeline that produced the data, and runs only when a human releases it.

story.name: Data Migration
story.description: This story specifies the requirements for ChatHealthy.ai's migration of published data from the pipeline cluster to the front-end cluster. A migration moves collections from ChatHealthyDataPipelines.PipelinePublicHealthData to ChatHealthyFrontEnd.PublicHealthData. A collection arrives under the name it left with. Nothing is transformed in transit. Migration is the only path by which data reaches the front-end cluster. It is separate from the pipeline that produced the data, and runs only when a human releases it.

requirement.name: A migrated collection keeps its name
requirement.requirement: Every collection present in ChatHealthyFrontEnd.PublicHealthData as the result of a migration carries the same name it had in ChatHealthyDataPipelines.PipelinePublicHealthData.

requirement.name: Migration is the only way data reaches the front-end cluster
requirement.requirement: No process other than a migration writes to ChatHealthyFrontEnd.PublicHealthData.

requirement.name: A migration runs only after a human releases it
requirement.requirement: Every migration MUST be preceded by a recorded human sign-off. The sign-off is taken at the operator's workstation. The implementing service MUST attest to this sign-off with evidence prior to execution of a migration.

requirement.name: A migration never alters or removes what is already there
requirement.requirement: No migration changes or removes any document, collection or index that existed before it ran. This binds the implementing service absolutely; nothing it is asked to do permits an exception.

requirement.name: A collection that already exists at the destination stops the migration
requirement.requirement: An implementing service that finds its target collection already present in ChatHealthyFrontEnd.PublicHealthData MUST abend. Prior to the abend it MUST: (a) raise an exception; (b) log a detailed narrative of the error including the collection name it found. It MUST NOT write, append to, or in any way alter the existing collection.

requirement.name: Every collection is reached through an instance of the one class that realizes this story
requirement.requirement: Within the implementing service, every access to data is made on behalf of exactly one named collection, and no access is made otherwise. The operator's workstation makes no such access.

requirement.name: The class constructor takes the collection name and nothing else
requirement.requirement: The constructor of the class that realizes this story accepts exactly one argument, the collection name.

requirement.name: The collection name is the only value assigned to the class from outside it
requirement.requirement: No variable on the class that realizes this story is assigned externally other than the collection name.

requirement.name: One file performs the migration
requirement.requirement: Exactly one file in the repository performs migration, and no other file does any part of it.

requirement.name: An engineering rule guarantees the code meets this story
requirement.requirement: An engineering rule parses the migration file with an LLM and guarantees that every requirement of this story is enforced by the code. A file that does not satisfy every requirement is not committed.

requirement.name: Zero trust - the migration's identities exist and are constrained to this story alone
requirement.requirement: Two actors take part: the operator's workstation makes the request, records an approval and verifies the software meets the requirements. The implementing service moves the data observing the rules as specified in these requirements.

requirement.name: The migration file is declared in the deployment manifest at its actual path
requirement.requirement: deployment_architecture.json declares the file that performs the migration under exactly one deployment target and one package, and the source_location it declares is that file's actual repository-relative path. A commit in which the file is undeclared, is declared in more than one place, or is declared at a path that is not where the file is, is not made.

requirement.name: A migration of a collection that is not there is refused and reported
requirement.requirement: An implementing service invoked against a collection that is not present in ChatHealthyDataPipelines.PipelinePublicHealthData MUST NOT report success. It MUST raise, and MUST record the refusal in the log naming the collection asked for.

requirement.name: DataTransferServiceToConfirmApproval
requirement.requirement: The implementing service is given the identity of the human's approval when it is asked to work. It reads that approval and confirms it releases this work; an identity naming no approval, or an approval that does not release this work, stops the transfer. Having confirmed it, and before doing any work, the service records its own acknowledgement of that approval alongside it.

requirement.name: Service Must Do Only One Job at a Time
requirement.requirement: If an invocation of the Data Migration service is made while a job is running, the second invocation MUST immediately abend and log the failure.
